sources.title: Vickers Wellington NZ-N (WMR-40191)
sources.summary: IWM entry for the brick and bronze plaque memorial on Darwell Hill, Netherfield. Names the maintainer as Stanislaw Jozefiak and the Polish Air Force Association Trust, and says it was unveiled on 27 May 2001, privately sponsored, designed and built by Mr Jozefiak. No names are listed; the inscription gives counts only.

sources.title: R1392 (NZ-N) 28th May 1941
sources.summary: Blog account of the loss of R1392 on a raid on Boulogne. Hit by flak in the port engine, crashed at Darwell Hole near Brightling, Sussex (the squadron record book says Kent). Lists four dead, one man missing after baling out, and two injured survivors including Jozefiak, who later built a memorial.

paragraphs.text: A Wellington of 304 Polish Squadron, R1392, was hit by flak in the port engine during a raid on Boulogne in May 1941 and crashed at Darwell Hole near Netherfield. Four of the crew were killed and two injured men survived. One more man baled out and was never found.
The memorial is a brick wall with a bronze plaque and a bronze Polish eagle. It was unveiled on 27 May 2001. Survivor Stanislaw Jozefiak sponsored, designed and built it.

IWM lists the Polish Air Force Association Trust as maintainer. A War Memorials Online comment says an annual service is held on the last Sunday of May, led by members of the Royal British Legion. We have not confirmed who looks after the memorial today.

notes: This is the same physical memorial and crash (Wellington R1392 NZ-N) as record wellington-r1392-crash (IWM 108829); IWM 40191 for this record. Custodian: IWM (S1) names Mr Jozefiak and the Polish Air Force Association Trust, but gives no date and Mr Jozefiak is described as a crash survivor from 1941, so current upkeep is unverified. WMO (S2) comment says Royal British Legion members lead the annual service; unattributed and undated, community-grade. Parish: Netherfield is in Battle civil parish (Wikipedia, S4) and Battle Town Council has a Netherfield ward (S5, search summary only); the 304 Squadron blog places the crash near Brightling and Art UK search snippet says Dallington, so the memorial's exact civil parish is not confirmed and needs checking with the council. Crash night: inscription says 27/28 May, blog says 28 May. Crew names from the blog only (single source), so not entered as crew claims. Sussex Express / Hastings Observer articles returned 403 and were not read. IWM 108829 page returned an error.
